content: The Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality: First Addendum to the Fourth Edition was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2017. The guidelines aim to protect public health by addressing drinking-water quality. They provide a comprehensive framework for risk management, covering the entire water supply chain from catchment to consumer. The guidelines emphasize achievable practices, sound regulations, and effective management approaches applicable to countries of varying income levels. They also summarize the health implications of contaminants in drinking water and the role of risk assessment and management in disease prevention and control. The first addendum to the fourth edition updates the guidelines with new evidence and clarifications. Key changes include new risk assessments and guideline values for substances such as dichlorvos, dicofol, and perchlorate, as well as revised assessments for barium, bentazone, diquat, and MCPA. Additional guidance is provided on microbial risk assessment, lead monitoring, and water treatment performance. References to supporting documents published after the fourth edition are also included. The guidelines are primarily intended for water and health regulators, policymakers, and their advisors to assist in developing national policies and regulations. They are also used as a resource by other stakeholders for information on water quality, health, and management strategies. The preparation of the first addendum involved contributions from hundreds of experts over more than five years. The document acknowledges the efforts of individuals and working groups specializing in microbial, chemical, and risk management aspects. Financial support from various international organizations and governments, including Australia, Singapore, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States, is also recognized.
